01 / The need

Useful information.
Accessible practice.

The project needed a central place for families to explore school information, find parent guidance and reach the school, alongside supplementary activities learners could use at home.

I approached it as a public information and learning website. The first version prioritises clear navigation, grade-based resources and downloads, while allowing the school to supply and approve further content.

02 / My contribution

From public pages to learning tools.

I designed and developed the responsive website, organised its content, built the learning interactions and connected its custom domain and deployment workflow.

01

School and parent information

Public pages for school information, parent guidance, notices, calendar, contact details and downloads. Notices and dates are added when supplied by the school.

02

A bilingual learning hub

160 English and Sepedi activities, with 20 activities for each grade from R to 7. Grade, subject and topic filters help families find relevant practice.

03

Printable learning resources

PDF and editable Word worksheets, with separate answer guidance, let families use resources away from the screen.

04

Quiz achievement certificates

Eligible Grade 4-7 quiz results at 70% or above can generate a PDF certificate with the learner's entered name, school name and badge. Certificates are learning acknowledgements, not formal school qualifications.

03 / Design decisions

Make the next step clear.

Organise around visitor needs

Parent guidance, learning resources and contact information have clear routes of their own. On smaller screens, an opening and closing side menu keeps navigation accessible.

Start with the learner's grade

Filtering by grade, subject and topic keeps a large activity collection manageable. Worksheets and separate answers support practice followed by checking.

Use English and Sepedi

The learning hub reflects the language needs of its audience. Sepedi materials are marked for teacher review rather than presented as fully validated translations.

Publish only supplied information

Pages distinguish available resources from official school notices and dates that have not yet been supplied. This avoids filling gaps with invented school information.

04 / Engineering approach

A maintainable public website.

HTMLCSSJavaScriptGitHub PagesGitHub Actions

I used a static front end with browser-based quiz, worksheet and certificate generation. The public learning features work without learner accounts or a hosted database.

Source changes are tracked in GitHub, and GitHub Actions publishes the website to GitHub Pages. The custom subdomain provides a stable address for the school website.

Scope decision: a staff dashboard and database-backed administration are deferred. School content can be updated in the website source until that later phase is agreed.

05 / Outcome and next steps

Live, useful and evolving.

The delivered website combines a public school information structure with a bilingual learning hub, downloadable resources and interactive quizzes.

This describes the implemented features. No visitor-growth, attainment or learning-impact claims are made without measured evidence.

  • Continue adding school-approved information and supplied staff profiles.
  • Arrange teacher review of activities, answer guidance and Sepedi translations.
  • Populate official notices and calendar entries as the school supplies them.
  • Review mobile usability and resource accuracy as the site develops.

06 / Reflection

Content is part of the product.

This project demonstrates how public information and learning tools can share one accessible interface. A live website also needs a clear way to distinguish completed functionality from content still awaiting approval.

My ongoing focus is keeping the resources organised, the information accurate and the code ready for future improvements.
